stories.headline: Oscar’s Week 8 predictions are live
stories.body: Zach and Baby Abdo meet in the Game of the Week, Hogies and Bob play for first place, and Tyler faces the players he traded to Sean. Plus Oscar’s 12-leg TD parlay, with Jahmyr Gibbs as the golden leg.

stories.historic: First three-team trade in league history
stories.headline: History made: the first three-team trade
stories.body: Tyler, Tyriese and Shmoody just swapped 11 players in the first three-team trade in Villains history. Tyler lands Brock Bowers and Javonte Williams, Shmoody gets Puka Nacua and Derrick Henry, and Tyriese walks away with five starters including James Cook, D'Andre Swift and Tee Higgins.

stories.headline: Oscar’s Week 9 predictions are live
stories.body: Zach and Mo climb the ladder for the Smoke Boy Championship in the Game of the Week, Hogies hunts Marissa, and Tyriese and Shmoody settle the three-team trade. Plus Oscar’s 12-leg TD parlay, with Jahmyr Gibbs as the golden leg again.

sides.note: Collin trades A.J. Brown (WR18) for Jameson Williams (WR26), who scored 14 points a game in Detroit before this. The cheaper of the two, which is not usually what one shops for.
Baby Abdo gets the bigger name and the bigger value. Brown has only 6.4 points a game in New England, so this is a bet on a reputation. Reputations, unlike receivers, rarely pull a hamstring.

trades.headline: History: the first three-team trade
trades.historic: First three-team trade in league history

sides.note: Tyler sent three players (James Cook, Jalen Coker and Kyle Monangai) and came back with two better ones: Brock Bowers, the TE2, and Javonte Williams, the RB9. Consolidation is the only form of subtraction that makes a man richer, and an elite tight end is the rarest thing in this league.

Tyriese gave up the best player in the deal, Puka Nacua, but came away with five starters: Cook, Swift and Higgins fill his lineup, and Coker gives him cover. One injury no longer wrecks his week, and when Mike Evans returns he will have one of the deepest benches in the league. Quantity has its own quality.

Shmoody took the prize of the deal, Puka Nacua (WR2), plus Derrick Henry, five days after acquiring Swift and Higgins and immediately spending them. Going from Bowers to LaPorta at tight end is the price of the jewel, and at 1–6 he can no longer afford to be patient.
Collin sends DeVonta Smith (WR20, 17.2 a game) away for Josh Downs and $55 of FAAB. FAAB is lovely in December, but in October it does not score.
Tyriese adds a third WR1-type to his new depth chart for a bench piece and some loose change. Smith is questionable this week, which is the only fine print.
Collin turns a waiver-wire quarterback into $8 of free FAAB. Free money is the only kind that never disappoints.
Tyriese paid $8 for Kyler Murray and released him 25 seconds later. Whatever this was, it was not about Kyler.

cover.headline: The League Is at War
cover.dek: Twelve teams, one battlefield. The three-team trade debuts, Hogies and Bob fight for first, Tyler faces his old players and two teams claw their way out of the Toilet Bowl. Week 8 predictions, analysis and Oscar’s picks.

games.title: Zach vs. Baby Abdo: Can Abdo Beat His Old Amon-Ra?
games.lineText: (5–2) Zach - Trade God (−130) vs. (3–4) Abdo - Beat the case (+110)
games.spreadText: Spread: Zach −3.5 | Total: 254 | Projection: Zach 128.9 - Abdo 125.2
story: Two weeks ago, Abdo traded Amon-Ra St. Brown to Tyler. Tyler flipped him to Zach a week later. On Sunday, Abdo finally sees him again, wearing the wrong jersey. Amon-Ra is questionable, and Abdo is hoping it stays that way.

Zach is 5–2 and has won his last two, including Sean's profile picture. His playoff odds are 94%. The Trade God has made more deals than anyone except Tyler, and most of them have worked. Bijan Robinson is projected for 21, Amon-Ra and Luther Burden, both from the Tyler blockbuster, give him a pair of starting receivers, and Dallas Goedert holds down tight end. Since Zach puts a deal together every week, the lineup will probably look different again by Sunday.

Abdo is 3–4, and his playoff odds are 15%. He has won two straight and has been building all season: Bucky Irving, George Pickens and DK Metcalf from Tyler, and A.J. Brown last night for Jameson Williams. Omar Cooper Jr. is averaging 22.5 a game. Lamar Jackson is questionable, but Jordan Love is on the bench in case the baby needs a babysitter. A loss puts him at 3–5, and at that point the playoffs are mostly a rumor.
The last two times these two met, they split. Zach won 138.84–106.62 in Week 2 last year, and Abdo got him back 124.24–110.04 in Week 13. The fans like Abdo 4–1. The sportsbook doesn't.

watch.text: The best projection in the game and the reason the Trade God is favored.
Questionable. If he plays, the baby has a chance. If he doesn't, Jordan Love babysits.

locker: Zach
I collect players. Abdo gave one away. Sunday I'll explain why that was a mistake.
Abdo
Amon-Ra knows what he did. Mo set the record against me. Shmoody lost to me. Zach is next.
games.oscarNote: Oscar is picking against the fans and siding with the man who has Bijan. If Amon-Ra sits, Oscar reserves the right to deny he ever said so.

games.title: Hogies vs. Sgt. Bob: Who Owns First Place?
games.lineText: (6–1) Hogies - White Tyriese (+180) vs. (5–2) Bob - Shedeur Stay, Shedeur Go (−220)
games.spreadText: Spread: Bob −14 | Total: 212.5 | Adjusted Projection: Bob 128.7 - Hogies 114 (with Hogies' bye-week replacements)
story: First place is on the line. Hogies is alone at the top at 6–1 and has won three straight. Bob is a game back at 5–2. He has also scored 982 points to Hogies' 980, so the man in first is chasing the man with the better team on paper. If Hogies wins, he goes to 7–1 and opens up a two-game lead. If Bob wins, they're both 6–2, and Bob takes first on points.

Hogies has picked a bad week to lose half his lineup to byes. Christian McCaffrey, Chris Olave, Jaylin Noel and Jordan Watkins all have the week off, and so do most of the players on his bench. He'll be shopping on the waiver wire by Sunday. What he has left is good, though. Dak Prescott is projected for 22.7, Trey McBride is the best tight end in the league that doesn't belong to Tyler, and Chuba Hubbard has quietly averaged 18 a game. The student has become a teacher in the standings, but this week he's a substitute teacher.

Bob has Jaxon Smith-Njigba, who is averaging 28 points a game and is the most dangerous receiver in the league. Kyren Williams adds 19.6 a game, and Drake London and Denzel Boston fill out a receiving room that would make most teams jealous. The only question mark is at quarterback, where Malik Willis is starting and hasn't played a down for him yet.
Bob has owned this matchup. He beat Hogies 166.94–91.14 in Week 6 last year and won again in Week 15, 141.68–132.48. The fans like Bob 4–1.

watch.text: With four starters on bye, the tight end has to play like a wide receiver and a running back at once.
28 points a game. The most dangerous receiver in the league, and Hogies has nobody to match him.

locker: Hogies
Byes don't scare me. I've been winning with backups all year. Bob's points don't count on the standings page.
Bob
Enjoy the view from first place, Hogies. It's about to be a lot shorter.
games.oscarNote: First place is a lovely address, but Hogies is only renting it. Bob has the lease, the furniture and Jaxon Smith-Njigba.

games.title: Tyler vs. Sean: Can Tyler Beat His Old Team?
games.lineText: (3–4) Tyler - Dolo’s cell mate (+405) vs. (5–2) Sean - CEEEDEEEZZZZ nuts (−555)
games.spreadText: Spread: Sean −30 | Total: 250.5 | Adjusted Projection: Sean 140.9 - Tyler 122.4 (line set before the three-team trade)
story: Sean's team is named after CeeDee Lamb, and Tyler is the one who traded him there. Before Week 1, Tyler sent CeeDee to Sean for Kenneth Walker. A week later, he sent Walker to Sean too. On Sunday, Tyler faces the two best players he's ever traded away, both wearing the same jersey. Walker is averaging 24.6 a game and CeeDee 22.2. Zay Flowers went to Sean and came back, and Joe Burrow arrived from Zach. Half of Sean's team has a receipt with Tyler's name on it.

Tyler is 3–4, has lost two straight and has lost on the final play three times this season. His playoff odds were 25% before Tuesday night, when he made the first three-team trade in league history to land Brock Bowers and Javonte Williams. With Williams, Flowers and Bowers, Tyler finally has the firepower to match Sean's big three. Jared Goff runs the offense, and Makai Lemon and Antonio Williams are his flex plays. The questions are Ladd McConkey and Jeremiyah Love, who are both questionable. The sportsbook set this line before the trade, which is why it reads like an insult.

Sean has scored 998 points, the most in the league, and he's 5–2 even after losing his profile picture to Zach last week. His big three are Walker, CeeDee and Joe Burrow, and Jonathan Taylor makes them a big four. His only soft spots are DJ Moore and Zach Charbonnet, who are both questionable.
Tyler has the history on his side. He beat Sean twice last year, 154.08–98.84 in Week 1 and 123.22–99.94 in Week 12. The fans like Sean 4–1.

watch.text: The prize of the three-team trade makes his debut. Tyler needs him to play like the TE1 on day one.
Averaging 24.6 a game since Tyler sent him over. Every point is a reminder.

locker: Tyler
Sean doesn't have a team. He has my old team. I know every one of those guys' weaknesses.
Sean
Thanks for CeeDee. Thanks for Walker. Thanks in advance for the win.
games.oscarNote: Tyler built a better team this week, but Sean built his out of Tyler's old one. Oscar is sad to report that the original still beats the remake.

games.title: Tyriese vs. Mo: Can Depth Beat the Beast?
games.lineText: (3–4) Tyriese - Welcome to Loveland 🫶 (+180) vs. (3–4) Mo - Beazy (−220)
games.spreadText: Spread: Mo −14 | Total: 258 | Adjusted Projection: Mo 139.5 - Tyriese 122.6
story: Both are 3–4, and the winner reaches .500. Mohammed holds the sixth playoff spot on points, and Tyriese sits just behind him. A loss doesn't end anyone's season, but it does start the countdown.

Tyriese spent Tuesday night rebuilding his roster. In four trades, he added James Cook, D'Andre Swift, Tee Higgins, Jalen Coker and DeVonta Smith, and briefly Kyler Murray, for about 25 seconds. This is the debut of the new Loveland. Caleb Williams leads it, Cook and Swift share the backfield, and Higgins, Coker and Stefon Diggs make up the receivers. The team runs five deep at receiver and running back. What it doesn't have anymore is Puka Nacua, and on a big week, a superstar wins games that depth can't.

Mohammed has won three straight and is the hottest team in the league. He set the league record with 196.10 against Abdo and has gone 3–0 since. Josh Allen is back from his bye, and Ja'Marr Chase and Justin Jefferson are both healthy. Both of those receivers came over in trades, and Jefferson came from Tyler. Malik Nabers and Isaiah Likely are on bye, but his bench covers both spots. At full strength, this might be the most talented team in the league, and he's no longer playing without a quarterback.
Last year, Tyriese beat Mohammed 179.12–130.68 in Week 4. The fans like Mohammed 4–1.

watch.text: His third team in a week. Tyriese gave up Puka to get him, so he'd better feel at home fast.
Back from the bye. Last week Mo had no quarterback; this week he has the best one in the game.

locker: Tyriese
Mo has three stars. I have ten starters. Do the math.
Mo
I set the record without a quarterback. Now I have one. Welcome to Loveland? Welcome to the beast.
games.oscarNote: Depth is a comfort in October, but stars win in November. Mohammed has three, and Tyriese traded his only one away on Tuesday.

games.title: Collin vs. Tim: Can the Annoyance Survive the Coffey Shop?
games.lineText: (3–4) Collin - Annoyance of the league (+165) vs. (4–3) Tim - The Coffey Shop (−200)
games.spreadText: Spread: Tim −12 | Total: 264.5 | Adjusted Projection: Tim 139.8 - Collin 118.9
story: This is the new guys' game. Collin took over Jordan's team this year, and Tim took over Ryan's. Neither has had a full season to earn a reputation, and both have spent this one making a name in the trade market. Tim is 4–3 with playoff odds of 74%. Collin is 3–4 at 36%, and a loss would make it feel a lot lower.

Collin has been the league's busiest trader after Tyler, and on Tuesday night he made three more deals. He added Jameson Williams and Josh Downs, plus $63 in FAAB. Last week Jahmyr Gibbs sat on his bench. This week Gibbs starts, and at 28.5 points a game he's the best running back in the league. Kirk Cousins has averaged 18.8 since arriving, Tony Pollard is steady, and Germie Bernard has quietly put up 15.7 a game. Breece Hall is questionable again. Collin has also been unlucky: 975 points have been scored against him, the second-most in the league. He's a better team than his record says.

Tim's best move came in Week 4, when he got Bo Nix and $100 of FAAB for Patrick Mahomes. Since then, he's built a deep, balanced team. Trevor Lawrence is projected for 21.4, Ashton Jeanty and Chase Brown share the backfield, and Christian Watson, Matthew Golden and Parker Washington are all averaging more than 15 a game. His one weak spot is at tight end, where Kyle Pitts is averaging 5.7 points a game. Golden and Jaylen Waddle are both questionable.
These two have never played each other. The fans like Tim 4–1.

watch.text: 28.5 a game and out of the lineup last week. Collin will not make that mistake twice.
The engine of the Coffey Shop. If he gets going early, Collin's comeback math stops working.

locker: Collin
They call me the annoyance of the league. Tim's about to find out why.
Tim
I took Mahomes out of my lineup and got better. Imagine what I'll do to Collin.
games.oscarNote: Collin has the best player on the field and the worst luck in the league. On Sunday, Oscar expects the luck to win.

games.title: Marissa vs. Shmoody: Who Gets Off the Bus?
games.lineText: (1–6) Marissa - Tuten on my Little Saq (−220) vs. (1–6) Shmoody - I Can’t Breathe (+180)
games.spreadText: Spread: Marissa −13.5 | Total: 253.5 | Adjusted Projection: Marissa 134.0 - Shmoody 116 (line set before the three-team trade)
story: The two 1–6 teams play for the right to not be alone in last place. The loser falls to 1–7. The winner escapes the basement, at least for a week. Both are down to playoff odds of 2% and 4%, and the sportsbook makes them the top two favorites for the Toilet Bowl.

Last year, Shmoody won the whole league. Now he's 1–6, has lost three games by less than a touchdown, and has had enough of waiting. Over five days, he traded for D'Andre Swift and Tee Higgins, then sent them away again to land Puka Nacua and Derrick Henry in the three-team trade. Both debut on Sunday. Geno Smith is averaging 23.5 a game, more than almost any quarterback in the league. The rest of the lineup is the problem: Blake Corum, Rome Odunze and Ja'Kobi Lane aren't scaring anyone. The sportsbook set this line before the trade, so it still prices Shmoody without Puka.

Marissa has scored 807 points, the fewest in the league, and 1,005 have been scored against her, the most. Some of that is her team and some of it is bad luck. Drake Maye has been solid, Tetairoa McMillan is averaging 16.2, and Bhayshul Tuten, her team's namesake, is averaging 14.7. The other half of the name has been the problem: Saquon Barkley is averaging 7.6 a game and is questionable again. She also has Patrick Mahomes sitting on her bench, which is a sentence that should never apply to a 1–6 team.
Last year Marissa beat Shmoody 111.24–106.20 in Week 11. The fans like Shmoody 4–1.

watch.text: He has run in a touchdown two weeks straight. Marissa needs a third.
The prize of the three-team trade debuts. The champion is betting the season on him.

locker: Marissa
Everybody keeps scoring 160 on me. Shmoody doesn't have 160 in him.
Shmoody
I'm still the champion. Puka just got here. The basement is for Marissa.
games.oscarNote: The fans believe in the champion and Oscar respects the sentiment. But Marissa has the better lineup, and Shmoody has the better excuses.

parlay.headline: Twelve legs, three debuts, one golden boy
parlay.intro: One anytime touchdown from every team. Quarterbacks only count if they run one in.
picks: 28.5 points a game and finally back in the lineup. The surest thing on the slip.
The Trade God's one untouchable. Atlanta gives him the ball at the goal line.
Green Bay's goal-line back. Abdo needs a touchdown more than anyone in the Game of the Week.
Bob's touchdown machine near the end zone, and a safer bet than JSN to find paydirt.
With McCaffrey on bye, Hogies' backfield belongs to him.
Day one of the three-team era. Dallas's lead back should get the short ones.
Two touchdowns the last time Oscar picked him. Tyler would prefer he forget how.
Third team in a week, same end zone. Buffalo always finds him there.
Back from the bye and the best running quarterback in the league. Oscar has learned this lesson before.
Oscar missed on him in Week 5. Oscar does not hold grudges, only parlay slips.
Two straight weeks with a rushing touchdown. Oscar is going for three.
The champion's new back is 32 years old and has never once been stopped at the 1-yard line.
parlay.sign: Gibbs is the golden leg. Josh Allen is the danger leg, because Oscar's quarterback picks have gone 3-for-6. If all twelve cash, Oscar retires to the countryside.

cover.headline: The League's Judgment Day
cover.dek: The league is running out of excuses. Zach and Mo climb the ladder for the Smoke Boy belt, Hogies hunts from first place, Tyriese and Shmoody settle the three-team trade, and Tyler and Abdo fight for their playoff lives. Week 9 predictions, analysis and Oscar’s picks.

games.title: Zach vs. Mo: Who Climbs the Ladder for the Smoke Boy Championship?
games.lineText: (6–2) Zach - Trade God (−135) vs. (3–5) Mo - Beazy (+110)
games.spreadText: Spread: Zach −4 | Total: 285.5 | Projection: Zach 144.8 - Mo 140.6
story: The belt hangs over the ring and both men are on the ladder. The Smoke Boy Championship goes to whoever reaches it first, and the 285.5-point total is the highest of the week, so the sportsbook expects fireworks.

Zach is 6–2 and has won three straight, including a 126.28–84.90 win over Baby Abdo last week. His playoff odds are 99%. He's also the luckiest team in the league: only 897.5 points have been scored against him, the fewest of any team. Bijan Robinson leads the league's best backfield with 153 points and is projected for 23.2 this week. Amon-Ra St. Brown has 141 and is questionable. Jayden Daniels is projected for 18.6 at quarterback, and George Kittle is back from his bye at tight end. The Trade God has found a way every week, and the record shows it.

Mo is 3–5, which makes no sense. He has scored 1,125 points, the second-most in the league, and has had the second-most scored against him. Last week he put up 147.66 and still lost to Tyriese's 166.98. No one has been less rewarded for doing more. Josh Allen is projected for 22.4 and ran in a touchdown last week. Ja'Marr Chase and Justin Jefferson are the best receiver pair on the field, and Malik Nabers is back from his bye too. His playoff odds are still 80%, because the math knows something the standings don't.
The only time these two have met, Mo won 111.90–82.52 in Week 11 last season. The fans like Mo 6–2, the most lopsided vote of the week.

watch.text: 153 points and the league's best backfield. If he finds the end zone, the belt goes to the Trade God.
Ran one in last week. Mo has scored more than almost anyone; Allen is how he finally gets paid for it.

locker: Zach
Mo can have the points. I'll take the wins. That's how you get a belt.
Mo
I've scored more than everybody and lost to everybody. Somebody's paying for that Sunday, and it's the Trade God.
games.oscarNote: Luck is a fine thing until it runs out, and Zach has been borrowing it all season. Oscar expects Mo to finally climb high enough to collect the debt, and the belt.

games.title: Hogies vs. Marissa: The Hunt
games.lineText: (7–1) Hogies - White Tyriese (−145) vs. (2–6) Marissa - Tuten on my Little Saq (+120)
games.spreadText: Spread: Hogies −5.5 | Total: 259 | Projection: Hogies 132.4 - Marissa 126.8
story: Hogies is 7–1, has won four straight and sits two games clear in first. Last week he beat Bob with half his team on bye, four waiver pickups and an empty bench. This week the regulars are back: Christian McCaffrey is questionable but projected for 22.9, Chris Olave returns at 15.4, Dak Prescott is projected for 19.8, and Trey McBride and Chuba Hubbard give him two more steady starters. Behind them, though, the bench is held together with tape. Carnell Tate is out, and Romeo Doubs and Jordyn Tyson are on IR. His playoff odds are 99.9%, so this is about keeping the lead, not making the playoffs.

Marissa is 2–6, but she's coming off her best game of the season. She dropped 166.06 on Shmoody last week. She's also been the unluckiest team in the league: 1,127.54 points have been scored against her, the most of anyone. Drake Maye is projected for 21.0 and has run in a touchdown three weeks straight. Tetairoa McMillan is steady, and Patrick Mahomes is projected for 21.2 on her bench, so she may be the only manager with two starting quarterbacks. The problem is her injury report: Saquon Barkley, Travis Kelce, Garrett Wilson, Michael Wilson and Bhayshul Tuten are all questionable. Her playoff odds are 9%, and every win from here is a must.
These two split last season. Hogies won 103.02–93.86 in Week 3, and Marissa won 111.40–96.58 in Week 14. The fans like Hogies 5–2.

watch.text: Questionable. If he plays, the hunter has his biggest weapon back.
Three straight weeks with a rushing touchdown. Marissa needs him to keep running.

locker: Hogies
First place, four straight, and the bartenders know my name. Marissa's just another stop on the tour.
Marissa
Everybody's been scoring 160 on me all year. Last week I did it back. Hogies is next.
games.oscarNote: Marissa has the hot hand and two quarterbacks, but Hogies has first place and the habit of winning. Oscar has learned not to bet against a man the bartenders love.

games.title: Tyriese vs. Shmoody: Who Claims the Treasure?
games.lineText: (4–4) Tyriese - No Love in The Land (−125) vs. (1–7) Team Shmoody (+105)
games.spreadText: Spread: Tyriese −3 | Total: 269.5 | Projection: Tyriese 136.2 - Shmoody 133.5
story: Two weeks ago, these two were on opposite ends of the first three-team trade in league history. Tyriese gave up Puka Nacua and Derrick Henry and walked away with five starters. Shmoody went the other way, sending out D'Andre Swift and Tee Higgins five days after getting them. On Sunday, the trade plays itself out on the same field, and both sides will finally find out who won it.

So far it's been Tyriese. He's 4–4, and last week his new depth beat Mo 166.98–147.66, one of the best scores of the season. Caleb Williams is projected for 18.5, and Swift and Higgins, both from Shmoody, are each projected for 16.6. James Cook adds 15, and Mike Evans is questionable but could be back from injury, projected for 16.4. His playoff odds are 85%, and this is the kind of game that keeps him there.

Shmoody won the whole league last year. Now he's 1–7, has lost three straight and sits alone in last, with playoff odds of 2%. He does have the best player on the field: Puka Nacua is projected for 23.1. Nico Collins adds 17.8, and Henry is still Henry. Kyler Murray is questionable at quarterback, but Bryce Young is right behind him at 17.1. The team is good enough to win; it just hasn't.

Tyriese beat Shmoody 108.80–90.52 in the regular season last year, but Shmoody got the one that mattered. He knocked Tyriese out of the playoffs 162.40–134.30 in the quarterfinals on his way to the title. The fans like Tyriese 7–1.

watch.text: Traded away by Shmoody twice in five days. This is the revenge game.
The prize of the three-team trade and the best projection on the field.

locker: Tyriese
I gave him Puka and he still can't win. The trade's over, and so is his season.
Shmoody
Ask Tyriese what happened in the quarterfinals last year. I end seasons. Ask him about it Sunday.
games.oscarNote: Shmoody has the brightest star on the field and a champion's memory. Tyriese has five starters for every one of Shmoody's. Oscar expects arithmetic to beat nostalgia.

games.title: Bob vs. Collin: Race to the Playoffs
games.lineText: (4–4) Collin - Annoyance of the league (+245) vs. (5–3) Bob - Shedeur Stay, Shedeur Go (−305)
games.spreadText: Spread: Bob −20 | Total: 261 | Projection: Bob 140.5 - Collin 120.6
story: Last week Collin was a 17-point underdog against Tim and won 122.36–95.20. This week the sportsbook has made him a 20-point underdog, apparently to see whether he can do it twice. He's won two straight, he's 4–4, and his playoff odds are a coin flip at 49%.

Collin's case starts and ends with Jahmyr Gibbs. Gibbs has scored 195.8 points this season, and at 25.8 he's the highest-projected player in this game. Kirk Cousins is steady at 17.4, and Jameson Williams and Josh Downs, both from his busy trade night, are in the lineup. Behind them it gets thin, and with 1,070.88 points scored against him, Collin has had to beat good scores all year. He's done it the last two weeks.

Bob is 5–3 with playoff odds of 95%, and he's coming off a 101.90–91.14 loss to Hogies with Malik Willis at quarterback. He's done waiting on that: Brock Purdy is in and projected for 22.2. Jaxon Smith-Njigba has scored 219.96 points, the most of any receiver in the league, and is projected for 24. Drake London (19.0) and Kyren Williams (18.7) make it the deepest lineup on the field. Deebo Samuel, Denzel Boston and Alvin Kamara are all questionable, but Bob has enough to cover for them.
These two have never played each other. The fans are split 4–4, so the league isn't as sure as the sportsbook.

watch.text: 195.8 points this season and the highest projection on the field.
The league's top-scoring receiver, now with Brock Purdy throwing to him.

locker: Collin
Seventeen points last week, twenty this week. Keep adding points, I'll keep winning.
Bob
Collin got lucky once. I've got JSN and a real quarterback now. Lightning doesn't strike twice.
games.oscarNote: Collin has made a habit of embarrassing the sportsbook, and Oscar admires a good habit. But Bob has the best receiver in the league and finally a quarterback to throw to him. Oscar takes Bob to win, and Collin to cover.

games.title: Sean vs. Tim: The Assassin's Last Job
games.lineText: (6–2) Sean - CEEEDEEEZZZZ nuts (−230) vs. (4–4) Tim - The Coffey Shop (+190)
games.spreadText: Spread: Sean −15 | Total: 278 | Projection: Sean 146.3 - Tim 131.5
story: Sean has scored 1,138.14 points, the most in the league, and last week he added 139.58 to beat Tyler. Joe Burrow threw five touchdowns, ran in a sixth and put up 39.48. Sean has since called a press conference to demand apologies from everyone who laughed at the trade that brought Burrow over. He's 6–2, and his playoff odds are 99.7%. Now the 2024 champion wants a bye.

The lineup is the most complete in the league. Kenneth Walker is projected for 22.0, Burrow for 21.4, CeeDee Lamb for 20.2 and Jonathan Taylor for 17.5. DJ Moore is questionable, but the bench is deep enough that it doesn't matter. Every one of Sean's big four has scored at least 144 points this season.

Tim is 4–4, has lost two straight and is still recovering from last week, when he lost to Collin as a 17-point favorite. He's since changed his LinkedIn title from "Assassin" to "Assassin (retired)." His playoff odds are 54%, and a third straight loss would put him below .500 for the first time. He does have a lineup that can keep up: Trevor Lawrence is projected for 19.7, and Chase Brown, Christian Watson and Matthew Golden are all in the 15-to-16 range. Ashton Jeanty has scored 132.3 points but is projected for only 12.2. Watson and Emeka Egbuka are questionable.
These two have never played each other. The fans are leaning Sean, 4–3.

watch.text: The top projection on the league's best team.
The assassin needs his quarterback to pull the trigger.

locker: Sean
I'm still waiting on those apologies. Tim can go first.
Tim
The assassin's coming out of retirement for one last job. Sean's name is on the list.
games.oscarNote: Every assassin has one last job, but most of them have it planned better than this. Sean has the best team in the league and the patience of a man waiting for an apology. Oscar expects him to get the win instead.

games.title: Tyler vs. Abdo: Get Out of My Swamp!
games.lineText: (3–5) Tyler - Dolo’s cell mate (−120) vs. (3–5) Abdo - Beat the case (−100)
games.spreadText: Spread: Tyler −1.5 | Total: 253 | Projection: Tyler 127.2 - Abdo 125.8
story: This is the closest line of the week, and it's close for a reason. Both are 3–5, both have playoff odds under 15%, and the loser can start planning for the Toilet Bowl. The winner gets to keep pretending.

Tyler has lost three straight, including a 139.58–98.94 loss to Sean last week, and his therapist has reportedly quit after he spent their whole session drawing up a four-team trade on the whiteboard. The three-team trade did give him the core he wanted. Jared Goff is projected for 20.0, Brock Bowers for 18.7 and Javonte Williams for 18.4. Zay Flowers and Ladd McConkey round out the receivers, and Cam Skattebo is questionable. The lineup is good. The record is not.

Abdo has scored 920.58 points, the fewest in the league, and lost 126.28–84.90 to Zach last week. Some of his best players came from Tyler: Bucky Irving is projected for 17.6, and George Pickens is questionable. Jordan Love, last seen suing Abdo for unpaid babysitting wages, is projected for 17.3 at quarterback. A.J. Brown is questionable, and with only 19.1 points since arriving, the bet on his reputation hasn't paid off yet. Josh Jacobs and Tyler Warren give him enough to keep it close.
Their only meeting was last year in Week 8, when Tyler won 140.82–140.28, by 0.54 points. The fans lean Tyler 5–3.

watch.text: Tyler traded three players to get him. Time to earn it.
A former Tyler player, which makes this personal.

locker: Tyler
Abdo's playing my old players. I know exactly how good they are, which is why I traded them.
Abdo
Tyler gave me Bucky and Pickens and he's still trading. Sunday, I give him a reason to stop.
games.oscarNote: Last year these two were separated by half a point, and this year the sportsbook can barely tell them apart. Oscar gives the edge to the man with the better tight end, and urges him to put the whiteboard down.

parlay.headline: Gibbs goes for two
parlay.intro: One anytime touchdown from every team. Quarterbacks only count if they run one in. Last week: 8-for-12.
picks: 153 yards and a touchdown last week. Some picks are value plays. This one is just correct.
Everyone will take Bijan. Oscar takes the receiver who put up 23.7 two weeks ago and has quietly become Zach's favorite deep target.
Josh Allen cashed last week. This week the touchdown goes to the receiver, which is how it should have been all along.
Jaxon Smith-Njigba gets the yards. London gets the red zone. With Brock Purdy taking over, Oscar likes the big man in the end zone.
Walker and CeeDee get the headlines. Taylor gets the goal line. Against Tim, there will be plenty of goal line.
Jeanty's projection has gone soft. Golden has the speed to score from anywhere.
Back from his bye and rested. McCaffrey is questionable, so Oscar takes the receiver who's definitely playing.
Three straight weeks with a rushing touchdown. Oscar is going for four, because streaks are only interesting until they end.
The team used to be named after him. Now it's called No Love in the Land. Oscar expects the tight end to take that personally.
He cashed last week, and he has never once been stopped at the 1-yard line.
Bowers draws the coverage. Flowers gets loose. Oscar likes the receiver nobody's watching.
Only 19.1 points since arriving. Questionable this week. Oscar is betting on a reputation, which is either brilliant or the dumbest pick on the slip.
parlay.sign: Gibbs is the golden leg again, because he earned it. A.J. Brown is the danger leg, because somebody has to be. Seven receivers, three backs, a tight end and one quarterback with legs. Last week's slip went 8-for-12. This week Oscar is aiming for perfection, which he has never achieved and does not expect to.
